messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nebulacorp.com>, Emma Li <emma@cloudsuite.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC traffic handshake & next steps

Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we scope the POC: 

Summary of what we heard (from Nebula):
- Primary product surface: API for content personalization (real-time scoring + batch re-rank).
- Peak patterns: traffic driven by hourly campaign windows + event-driven spikes.
- Current infra: mixed cloud; willing to pilot on Redwood hosted endpoints.

Required items from Nebula to scope the POC:
1) Traffic matrix (RPS by endpoint over the day, mean token lengths per request, typical concurrency) — CSV is ideal.
2) Representative sample requests (10k combined sample with token-length distribution) — anonymized.
3) Success criteria: initial suggestion below — confirm or propose alternatives.

Our proposed POC scope (30 days):
- Ingest their traffic profile to run a synthetic soak and burst tests.
- Measure latency p50/p95/p99, successful generations per minute, and token-cost metrics.
- Two model variants: full-quality (fp16/quantized LLM) and cost-optimized (4-bit quant).

Suggested success criteria (draft):
- Sustained baseline: 120 RPS sustained for 15-min window with p95 <= 250 ms (in-region).
- Burst tolerance: tolerate 650 RPS bursts (up to 60s) with p99 <= 900 ms and no more than 0.5% error rate (timeouts/5xx).
- Token cost target: <= $0.0018 per generated token for the cost-optimized run (for benchmark input set).
- Quality regression: automated eval on 500 prompt pairs, no more than 5% degradation in top-line quality metrics vs baseline model.

Data we need from you by EOD Friday (2026-11-06): traffic CSV, 10k anonymized samples, and confirmation on the three success criteria above. File names / attachments are fine (we've attached a POC scope template).

Next steps / owners:
- Nebula: supply traffic CSV + samples (Alex) — due 2026-11-06 EOD.
- Redwood: create synthetic traffic harness + run initial soak (Ben) — scheduled to start 2026-11-09 once samples are in.
- Eval/quality: Karthik to own automated evals and regression checks.
- Ops contact: Grace to coordinate any firewall/VPC access for private tests.

Attachments: POC_scope_doc.pdf (template), call_recording_link.txt

Thanks — want to keep this lightweight; if any of the success thresholds above look off, call it out in your reply and we’ll adjust.

—Camila

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nebulacorp.com>

Cc: Emma Li <emma@cloudsuite.com>, procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC traffic handshake & next steps

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. High level answers and an initial traffic sketch attached (nebulacorp_traffic_matrix.csv). Quick notes inline: 

- Baseline traffic: 80–130 RPS over the workday, average 95 RPS.
- Peak windows: two campaign peaks at 11:00–12:00 and 18:00–18:30 local time, where we see consistent surges up to 600–700 RPS for ~45–90s.
- Typical concurrency: our frontend opens ~350 concurrent sockets during peak windows; effective concurrency for inference requests is ~160.
- Token lengths: median input tokens 48, median generated tokens 120, 95th perc generated tokens ~420. Distribution attached in the CSV.
- Error tolerance: we can accept short-lived throttling but need <1% failed requests in a campaign window.

We can provide the 10k sample bundle (anonymized) by Friday EOD. One note on success criteria: the 120 RPS sustained baseline is fine, but p95 target of 250 ms sounds optimistic given our median generated token length (120). If the baseline model returns streaming responses, p95 <= 600 ms would be acceptable for us, p99 <= 1.2s during bursts. For the cost target, we'll accept benchmarking numbers post-run.

Attached: nebulacorp_traffic_matrix.csv (contains RPS by hour, token distribution), sample_manifest.txt (links to S3 bucket with samples).

On procurement: we'll loop in our buying team next week for terms.

—Alex
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering — NebulaCorp
alex.thompson@nebulacorp.com

Forwarding Alex's sketch — looks reasonable. High-level internal plan and owners so we can move quickly when files arrive: 

Evaluation plan (Ben/Karthik/Camila):
- Day 0–2: Validate sample format & sanity check token lengths (Camila).
- Day 3–6: Build synthetic traffic harness that mimics hourly seasonality and the 600–700 RPS 60–90s campaign spikes (Ben). Harness to support both real-time (persistent connections) and stateless HTTP.
- Day 7–14: Run baseline runs against full-quality model (target: gather p50/p95/p99 and token-cost metrics).
- Day 15–22: Run cost-optimized variant and A/B rerank evaluations.
- Day 23–30: Consolidate results, run automated quality eval (Karthik) and prepare a readout.

Concrete measurement plan:
- Latency windows: measure p50/p95/p99 for request time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token where applicable.
- Error budget: track 5xx+timeouts and keep <0.5% for baseline; <1% allowed in burst windows unless otherwise negotiated.
- Cost: estimate $/generated_token for the 10k sample set.

Owners:
- Camila: sample verification & customer coms.
- Ben: harness + soak/burst runs + runbook.
- Karthik: automated evals + quality thresholds.
- Grace: infra handoffs and any networking/VPC needs.

Next internal checkpoint: sync on Monday 2026-11-08 11:00 PT (15 minutes) to confirm harness config. If samples land Friday EOD we can stand up preliminary runs Monday afternoon.

Attachments referenced in Alex's email: nebulacorp_traffic_matrix.csv, sample_manifest.txt

—Ben

Alex — thanks for the CSV and manifest. We ingested the sample manifest and spot-checked distributions; everything looks good. A few clarifications and confirmed next steps: 

Clarifications based on your notes:
- We’ll treat your acceptable burst p99 at 1.2s as the upper bound during the campaign windows. Our run will report both time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token so you can validate streaming behavior.
- We'll cap allowed error rate to 1% during the two campaign windows you described (11:00–12:00, 18:00–18:30) and keep <0.5% for baseline windows. If throughput requires a temporary fallback, we’ll document degraded behavior in the runbook.

Confirmed plan & schedule: 
- Friday 2026-11-06: Nebula to confirm samples delivered (done).
- Monday 2026-11-09: Redwood to stand up harness and run quick sanity soak (Camila/Ben).
- Wednesday 2026-11-11: First full baseline run complete and preliminary metrics shared (Ben/Karthik).
- Monday 2026-11-16: Cost-optimized runs and quality evals complete; readout deck draft.

Immediate asks for kickoff: please share S3 read permissions for the sample bundle and a test API key or sandbox endpoint if available (Alex/procurement). If you prefer, we can route sandbox access through a short-lived pre-signed URL.

Can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff on Monday 2026-11-09 at 10:00 PT to walk through the harness parameters and define the exact campaign spike windows? I’ll send a calendar invite once Alex confirms.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—Camila
